findings.description: The R2-F3 fix replaced a CORRECT mechanism with an incorrect one and supplied an invalid proof for it. Three clauses are refuted by the measurement above. (1) 'that is not what empties src/a.sh out of the bound set HERE' is false: truncation runs FIRST (G.1's approve succeeds, which the fixture itself asserts) and is what removes src/a.sh; by the time line 675 executes the tracker is already empty, so the replacement adds the artifact to an empty file rather than displacing anything. (2) The offered proof, 'had truncation been the cause, bound would be 0; it is 1', is a non-sequitur, and Variant Y measures the counterfactual world directly: with `>>`, where truncation is unambiguously the only thing that could have removed src/a.sh, bound is still 1 — not 0. The conditional's own consequent is false in its own antecedent's world, so bound=1 does not discriminate between the two hypotheses at all. (3) 'note `>` not `>>`' presents the operator as load-bearing; it is immaterial, because `>>` yields a byte-identical tracker and an identical refusal. What is true is weaker and should be what the comment says: BOTH mechanisms are independently sufficient (had truncation not run, the `>` alone would still produce the miss), so this is overdetermination, and truncation is the one that actually fires first. The aggravating detail is that this text's own closing sentence names the defect it commits — 'a true conclusion resting on a false mechanism is the shape this release exists to refuse'. The conclusion (the miss is real, the re-seed at 767 is needed, H.3 measured the wrong refusal) remains TRUE and is not in question; only the attributed mechanism and its proof are wrong. Note for the record that round 2's own suggested remedy ('approve does truncate on success; it is simply not what produces the miss here') embedded this error, so it is inherited from my prior round, not invented by the author. Remedy: state the actual order (truncate, then replace), say the two causes are independently sufficient with truncation preempting, and delete the bound=0-vs-1 argument entirely rather than repairing it.

findings.description: 'collapses the whole restore-control tail with it — H.4 through H.6b, eight failures' attaches the count to a range that holds six. Eight is the correct MEASURED TOTAL, but reaching it requires adding H.3 and H.3b, and the sentence names only H.3 separately (never H.3b). Under the plain appositive reading — two comma-separated descriptions of the same referent, its extent and its size — the claim that H.4 through H.6b is eight failures is false by two. Under a charitable 'eight in total' reading it is true but misattached. I grade this MEDIUM rather than HIGH under the operator's stop rule because the number itself matches reality (a reader who re-runs the substitution sees exactly 8) and the mechanism is fully correct, so nothing about shipped gate behaviour is misstated; the error is which assertions sit inside the named range. The one-character remedy makes it unambiguously true: 'H.4' -> 'H.3', since H.3 through H.6b is exactly eight. Secondary, folded in here rather than filed separately: 'the whole restore-control tail' is itself loose for that range — only H.5/H.5b and H.6/H.6b carry RESTORE CONTROL in their own assertion text; H.4/H.4b are a different check (a verdict recorded against the OLD hash is refused at record time). As with R3-F1, round 2's own suggested wording proposed this exact phrasing ('H.4 through H.6b — measured: 8 failures'), so the miscount is inherited from my prior round.
